identity.fantasy: A reality-corroding time mage who layers long-lived effects until anomalies and impossible spell repeats begin feeding themselves.
identity.one_line: Timerend and other periodic effects constantly reduce the remaining cooldowns of damaging spells. The spec stacks Mind Melt, triggers Anomaly Spikes and Chromatic Shards, and enters Incarnation of Chaos for a volatile burst phase. Recent players describe it as almost entirely DoT-based and note that late talents materially change its form loop.

mechanics.core_loop: Keep Timerend and Melt Reality working, build Mind Melt through periodic pressure, use Anomaly Spikes to accelerate Chromatic Shard, and enter Incarnation of Chaos when its reset and damage window can be exploited.
mechanics.single_target: Long-lived periodic effects create cooldown reduction and proc opportunities; Chromatic Shard and Incarnation of Chaos turn that setup into direct burst.
mechanics.aoe: Shifting Chaos spreads part of Chromatic Shard and Anomaly Spike damage, while later Timerend interactions add another pack payoff. Much of the setup still begins on a primary target.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: DoTs continue working while moving, but changing targets can abandon Mind Melt stacks and other accumulated setup. Chaos Fusion later allows Chromatic Shard during Incarnation movement.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Chronomancer roots, slows, knockback, healing, and temporal defenses support a kite-and-let-DoTs-work pattern reported by current leveling players.
mechanics.group_utility: Infinite Horizon supplies a non-stacking party damage aura, alongside the base Chronomancer control and haste toolkit.

failure_modes.text: Refreshing or replacing long effects without regard to target lifetime spends mana on damage that may never tick.
Changing targets early loses accumulated Mind Melt and Chromatic Shard acceleration.
Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: dots continue working while moving, but changing targets can abandon mind melt stacks and other accumulated setup.

cautions: Current players report early mana pressure

append_claims.text: A July leveling discussion reports early Infinite mana pressure; replies recommend Spirit and mana tools, note improvement around level 32, and advise letting periodic effects finish enemies while kiting.
append_claims.notes: Small anecdotal sample with differing experiences.

append_claims.text: Infinite loses efficiency when a target dies or is abandoned before its long periodic effects and stacked debuffs repay their setup cost.
append_claims.notes: The exact target-lifetime threshold is not measured.

append_claims.text: Players describe Infinite as an almost-all-DoT caster mixing instant cooldown DoTs with hard-cast DoTs that reduce those cooldowns before a large finisher.
append_claims.notes: Manually reviewed on 2026-08-06; anecdotal evidence is not treated as a power ranking.
